fills.notes: The three wheels are cosmic mechanisms turned by the King of Glory; the clause needs a locative for where the wheels are ‘found’ before being stirred by wind/water. ‘In the heights’ keeps the oldest cosmological register and matches the subsequent ‘up above all the mountains.’

The wheel’s sediment is cast into the inner sea ‘like’ something from the mountain; in correspondential physics, what is washed out of the star-wheel is a heavy, earthy precipitate. ‘Stone of the mountain’ (i.e., a rock falling) fits the weight/precipitate logic better than a liquid or living comparison.

The thought collects, binds, and fixes the sediment: the function is stabilization—making the precipitate a fixed base within the inner sea, preparing the later ‘constructed/moulded’ giant as residue-solidified. ‘As a foundation’ fits the mechanical-cosmic tone (not moral).

After listing seals of time (seconds→years) and of heaven (stars/zodiac), the sentence needs a closure indicating the totality of these impressions. This also prepares ‘He came into existence from them…’

The immediately prior context is the star-wheel and zodiacal turning; the ‘images…doctrines and counsels’ belong to that same astral mechanism. Restores the substrate’s impersonal astral-cosmology rather than any later communal/ethical source.
‘The sea also conceived him …’ expects the paired act: conception followed by bearing/bringing forth, before the clause about the sea’s role as sculptor/craftsman.

The phrase ‘for its part … it being his chief sculptor’ requires a verb of active formation assigned to the sea. ‘Fashioned’ keeps the craft register that immediately follows (‘sculptor…craftsman…sculpted’).
Keeps the existing editor’s fill; it matches the correspondential point: many stamped forms are reduced into one ultimate body.
Keeps the existing editor’s fill; it fits the process of many impressions becoming complete in one formed body.
The analogy concludes that the single body is constituted out of the many prior impressions; this bridges cleanly to ¶7 where the giant is ‘from many doctrines and counsels.’

The syntax needs an infinitival-purpose/causal connector after ‘disturb the sea’ leading into ‘a fullness and a … becomes’. ‘So that a…’ supplies the expected consequence construction; the surviving final ‘a’ is preserved as the article.
Paired opposites are demanded: the giant’s inhaling/disturbing produces alternating states in the sea—fullness vs lack. This matches the tidal/pulsation mechanics implied by ‘movement’.

‘becomes between his movement … purify’ needs the oscillatory medium linking his motion to the sea’s cleansing action. ‘Ebb and flow’ gives the natural correspondence of alternating influx/efflux that stirs and purifies sediments.
The final contrast ‘but the sea …’ expects the conclusion: although he draws power/life and disturbs, the net effect on the sea is purification/cleansing (as earlier: washing/loosening sediment).

assessment: Most gaps are structurally constrained by the chapter’s correspondential mechanics: astral sediment is cast down, fixed as a base, then re-formed as the sea giant bearing the seals of time and zodiac. The hardest restorations are in ¶12, where the preserved text is too fragmentary to recover exact wording; the proposed fills keep the oscillation/purification logic (influx/efflux → fullness/deficiency → cleansing) consistent with the oldest cosmological substrate.
